represents: The schedule-bound pod-sandbox starts of the same 3-hour window and staging cluster as k8s-cri-pod-sandboxes: one sandbox for each of the window's 36 CronJob runs (ledger-reconcile, db-backup and cert-expiry-report hourly, report-export every 30 min, index-compact every 20 min, session-gc every 15 min; restartPolicy OnFailure restarts a failed container inside the same pod, so a Job has one pod), started ~1-3 s after its scheduled minute; and a kubeadm control-plane upgrade (apply on k8s-cp-01, then node on k8s-cp-02 and k8s-cp-03) that starts each node's etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler static pod once with its new manifest (config.source file). Hits here are exact counts of those pods.
provenance: synthetic, written out once each (count 1, one sequence of literal sandboxes) because a finite schedule cannot be drawn independently without repeating a pod: shapes as in k8s-cri-pod-sandboxes (`crictl pods -o json` via detections/k8s/cri-pod-sensor.sh); the CronJob Job names (<cronjob>-<scheduled minute since the epoch>), Job uids and pod names/uids are the ones the k8s-audit-control-plane slice's cronjob-controller, job-controller and kubelet events use; Job pod labels per the batch/v1 Job controller; static pods per kubeadm (component/tier labels, config.hash = pod uid, advertise-address annotations), the order and pacing of `kubeadm upgrade` (etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, each after the previous is healthy). Sandbox ids and sub-second timings are random; names are fictional, addresses RFC1918.
adjacent_to: T1543.005/k8s_cri_static_pod_start.yml (expected to fire on the 12 kubeadm static pods of the upgrade)
